requirements.title: The set of external files existing for a program is processor dependent
requirements.definition: At any time, the set of external files that exist for a program is processor dependent, and a file may be known to the processor without existing for that program then.

pending.existing-external-file-set-processor-dep: No portable oracle may assume a particular ambient external file exists; future tests create their own files or use scratch files before relying on existence.

requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

S12.3.2-001 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: after a controlled delete of a conservative local name, INQUIRE(FILE=name, EXIST=...) observes that a processor-known character string need not denote an existing file for the program at that time.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

S12.3.2-001 I/O records/files fixture boundaries: These fixtures are single-image positive runtime observations over internal CHARACTER files, scratch external files, and conservative local named files created in the execution working directory and deleted by the program. They assert only exact integers/logicals/characters, LEN before character equality, IOSTAT zero, and equality with the named IOSTAT_END constant. They do not assert byte sizes, record marker layout, IOMSG text, numeric IOSTAT values, ambient file existence, path syntax beyond the chosen local names, preconnected file identity, coarray image interactions, stream/record correspondence, or required diagnostics for mismatched forms/nonexistent files. Remaining facets stay pending with their source-accounting rationale.

requirements.title: Creating and deleting files change file existence
requirements.definition: To create a file is to cause a previously nonexistent file to exist; to delete a file is to terminate the existence of the file.

requirements.title: Selected input/output statements may refer to files that do not exist
requirements.definition: CLOSE, ENDFILE, FLUSH, INQUIRE, OPEN, PRINT, REWIND, and WRITE statements are permitted to refer to a file that does not exist.

pending.close-may-reference-nonexistent-file: After CLOSE semantics are registered, use a controlled unit/file state and assert only portable success or named status permitted by CLOSE, not a numeric code.
pending.endfile-may-reference-nonexistent-file: After ENDFILE and preconnection rules are registered, reference a controlled nonexistent preconnected file and observe creation/endfile behavior if portable.
pending.flush-may-reference-nonexistent-file: After FLUSH semantics are registered, use IOSTAT initialized to a nonzero sentinel and assert only that the permitted reference is not rejected for nonexistence when a portable setup exists.
pending.print-may-reference-nonexistent-file: No portable single-image oracle for PRINT preconnection target existence; future tests must avoid assuming a terminal/printer file identity.
pending.rewind-may-reference-nonexistent-file: After REWIND semantics are registered, use a controlled unit state and assert only portable status, not position of a nonexistent external medium.
pending.write-may-reference-nonexistent-file: WRITE to a controlled preconnected or opened creation target and then read/inquire the created file where portable.

requirements.definition: No input/output statement other than the listed permitted statements shall refer to a file that does not exist.

requirements.title: WRITE, PRINT, or ENDFILE can create a nonexistent preconnected file
requirements.definition: Execution of WRITE, PRINT, or ENDFILE referring to a preconnected file that does not exist creates the file.

pending.write-creates-nonexistent-preconnected-f: Use a controlled preconnected unit only if a processor profile exposes one; then WRITE known data and INQUIRE existence. Without such a profile no portable oracle exists.
pending.print-creates-nonexistent-preconnected-f: No portable single-image oracle exists for PRINT target file existence because the preconnected output unit and medium are processor dependent.
pending.endfile-creates-nonexistent-preconnected: Use only if a controlled preconnected sequential file can be established; assert creation/existence and named endfile behavior, not a file name or status number.

requirements.title: A file created from a preconnected nonexistent file is image-distinct
requirements.definition: The file created by WRITE, PRINT, or ENDFILE on a nonexistent preconnected file is different from one preconnected on any other image.

pending.preconnected-created-file-different-acro: No single-image oracle exists; a future multiimage test must independently establish preconnection on each image and avoid assuming path-name identity.
